Project Title: Mars Explorer – An Integrated Mars Surface Exploration and Mission Planning Platform

Mars Explorer is a web-based platform designed to support future human exploration of Mars by combining information from multiple NASA science missions into a unified interactive interface. It provides layered views of the Martian surface, including terrain, elevation, thermal properties, mineralogical information, and scientific exploration targets. Users can explore selected regions, identify potential hazards, select destinations, and generate Marswalk route plans with estimated distances, travel durations, and risk indicators.

The project addresses NASA's challenge by bringing diverse planetary datasets together to help astronauts and mission planners make more informed decisions about exploration routes while identifying scientifically valuable locations along the way. By integrating surface conditions with scientific observations, Mars Explorer aims to balance mission safety and scientific discovery. It provides a foundation for a more efficient, data-driven approach to planning future Marswalks and supporting human exploration beyond Earth.

Project Details – Mars Explorer

Mars Explorer is a web-based Mars surface exploration and mission-planning platform designed to assist future astronauts in planning safe and scientifically productive Marswalks. It brings together different types of Martian surface information into a unified, interactive dashboard.

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

The platform allows users to explore selected Martian regions through an interactive map interface. It provides multiple data-layer options, including terrain, elevation, thermal properties, mineralogical information, and scientific exploration targets. Users can select destinations, examine potential terrain challenges, and generate a Marswalk plan displaying estimated route distance, travel duration, terrain complexity, and risk indicators.

The concept is designed around integrating information from NASA missions such as Mars Global Surveyor (MOLA), Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (HiRISE and CRISM), Mars Odyssey (THEMIS), and the Perseverance rover (MEDA).

2. What are its benefits?

  • Combines information from multiple NASA missions in one interface.
  • Makes complex planetary data easier to explore and understand.
  • Helps identify potential terrain challenges before planning a traverse.
  • Highlights scientifically interesting geological locations.
  • Supports route planning while considering both exploration objectives and potential risks.
  • Provides an expandable platform for incorporating additional Mars datasets.

3. What is the intended impact?

The intended impact is to support better-informed decisions during future human exploration of Mars. By connecting surface conditions, route information, and scientific opportunities, Mars Explorer aims to help astronauts plan more efficient Marswalks, reduce exposure to potential terrain hazards, and maximize scientific discoveries during limited exploration time.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed as a browser-based application using:

  • HTML5: Website structure and content.
  • CSS3: Responsive layout, styling, and dashboard design.
  • JavaScript: Interactive map layers, destination selection, and route-planning demonstrations.
  • NASA scientific datasets and mission resources: Identified as the intended sources for integrating Martian surface and environmental information.
  • GitHub and GitHub Pages: Version control, project hosting, and public website deployment.

No physical hardware is required because the project is a software-based platform.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creative aspect of Mars Explorer is its approach to bringing different scientific perspectives together in a single mission-planning environment. Instead of viewing terrain imagery, elevation information, thermal observations, and geological data separately, users can switch between different layers and understand how they contribute to an exploration decision.

It connects route planning with scientific discovery, allowing exploration destinations to be considered not only as locations to reach but also as opportunities to investigate the Martian environment.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The main factors considered during development include:

  • Terrain safety: Surface slopes, elevation variations, and rough terrain.
  • Scientific value: Geological formations and mineralogical observations worth investigating.
  • Route efficiency: Distance and estimated travel duration.
  • Data integration: Combining observations from different NASA missions.
  • Usability: Creating an intuitive interface that makes complex information accessible.
  • Scalability: Designing the platform to accommodate additional datasets and exploration regions.
  • Data reliability: Considering the source, resolution, observation time, and limitations of scientific measurements.

Overall, Mars Explorer aims to transform scattered planetary observations into a unified exploration-planning experience, helping bridge the gap between scientific data and practical human exploration.
